Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed slowdown in afternoon interaction window

Neha / Rishi — dug into the node-level telemetry and batcher logs. Key findings:
- Around 11:42 PT we had a short-lived surge of concurrent generation sessions from a third-party partner; that produced sustained KV-cache pressure on a subset of US-W serving pools.
- Autoscaler responded but the scale-up had a ~90s ramp during which continuous batching increased per-token latency for mid-length sequences.
- No CPU or GPU OOMs; memory pressure caused more frequent KV cache evictions which magnified latency for warmed sessions.

Short-term mitigations proposed:
1) Pin EdenWell traffic to a lower-concurrency dedicated pool (can be done as a temporary routing policy) — reduces contention.
2) Apply a conservative batching cap for your routes (max batch size 8) to control tail latency.
3) Enable prefix-KV pin for the most critical endpoints.

I'll draft the routing change and coordinate with infra to apply a controlled cap.

— Markus
Markus Klein

Hi Laura — follow-up and post-incident notes. Sorry again for the impact. Below is a concise recap and the long-term items we're committing to.

What happened:
- A transient spike from a partner workload on 2026-12-14 at ~11:40 PT caused KV cache pressure on a subset of US-W serving pools.
- Continuous batching increased while autoscaler ramped, driving p95/p99 increases for mid-length sequences for a ~25 minute window.

Immediate customer-facing actions we took:
- Pinned EdenWell traffic to a reserved pool (applied at 12:05 PT) — reduced p95 back to baseline within five minutes.
- Applied conservative batching cap (max batch size 8) for your routes — mitigated tail risk.
- Provided you with a list of affected request IDs and host traces (attached).

Longer-term commitments:
1) We'll add a route-level safety margin to avoid sudden autoscaler ramp contention in US-W. ETA: Q1 2027.
2) We will surface a customer-visible signal on prefix-cache eviction rates in the Console within the next six weeks so teams can see early warning signs.
3) We'll work with partners to add soft-throttles to noisy workloads and improve isolation policies.

Follow-up items for EdenWell:
- We recommend temporary rate smoothing for your heaviest endpoints during peak interaction windows.
- If you'd like, we can provision a low-cost dedicated pool for the next 30 days while we complete platform-side mitigations; Markus will provide COGS and estimated incremental pricing for procurement.
